## Quantization: Weights, Activations, and KV Caches {#sec-ch5}

::: {.callout-note title="Scaffold status"}
Scaffold only: drafting has not yet begun. This page records the approved plan for the chapter; it contains no teaching content, questions, answers, figures, worked examples or citations yet.
:::

**Purpose.** Separate number formats, scaling granularity and quantization methods, and explain what each changes in memory, speed and model behaviour.

**Prerequisites and planned recap.** Chapter 1 (critical batch size) and Chapter 2 (per-sequence KV accounting).

**Scope boundaries.** No quantization-aware training, FP8 training or FP4/microscaling formats. Every quantization method here changes numerics; quality evidence is reported with its conditions.

### Learning objectives

Planned outcomes (approved scope). By the end of this chapter you should be able to:

- Distinguish INT8/INT4 and FP8 formats from per-tensor, per-channel, per-token and per-group scaling, and from quantization methods.
- Explain why weight-only quantization helps bandwidth-limited decode and does not by itself reduce compute.
- Explain one weight-only, one weight-activation and one KV-cache method in depth, and compare others in a table.
- Read a quantization quality or speed claim against its stated conditions.
